page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM hypervisor virtualization. Powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz, it features 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, presenting 8 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) to the guest operating system. The instance is paired with 16.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache allocation includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached block storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core performance characteristics, placed within the top 10 percent for single-core stress-ng tests and the top 25 percent for Geekbench single-core and text processing workloads. Multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, fall into average ranges relative to comparable cloud instances. Instruction set capabilities include AVX-512, SHA-NI, and AES hardware acceleration. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 47.95 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth achieves 28.19 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 11.16 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measures 10.4 GB/sec.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio optimizes memory allocation for compute-bound tasks where per-core processing throughput takes precedence over large memory overheads. Lack of local NVMe storage requires external persistent storage solutions, introducing potential IOPS latency dependencies based on attached volume configurations. Given the high single-thread efficiency and dedicated vCPU allocation, the instance is well suited for CPU-focused execution, compilation tasks, web serving, API gateways, and light database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a dedicated 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 9T34 processor under the KVM hypervisor. Featuring an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, combined with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core. It lacks local disk storage and GPU hardware, depending on external storage and supplying 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU execution alongside strong single-threaded text processing scores, while multi-core metrics sit within standard industry averages. Supported hardware flags include AVX-512 vector extensions and AES cryptographic acceleration. The balance of high single-thread performance and a focused memory profile makes this instance suitable for web serving, software compilation, API routing, and intermediate compute workloads.
